# Fig. 1 — Benchmark one-line diagram

**Section 2.1** · the four-machine wind farm, its collector and the grid
connection.

**Status: `verified`.** Not a computed result: a drawing. Every quantity it
depicts is checked against the model below.

---

## This figure is not generated by the code

It is a hand-drawn schematic, kept as `system-one-line_AGC.pdf`. There is no
script that produces it and none is expected. What **can** be verified is that
what it depicts matches the model, and that is what this file is for.

## What the diagram must show to be correct

| Element | Model value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Machines | 4 | `CONFIG_MODEL.m:174` |
| Machine rating | 2 MW each, 8 MW total | derived from `S_b` |
| Machine-side voltage | 690 V line-to-line rms | `CONFIG_MODEL.m:151` |
| PCC voltage | 33 kV | figure |
| Step-up transformers | **two different ratings** | `CONFIG_MODEL.m:214` |
| Grid connection | Thevenin source behind `Z_grid` | `LINEAR_ANALYSIS.m:246-258` |

## The one thing a reader must take from it

**The transformers are not identical.** `SCR_transformer = [10 10 5 5]`, so G3
and G4 sit behind exactly twice the impedance of G1 and G2.

If the diagram is redrawn with four identical transformer symbols it becomes
wrong in the one way that matters, because that asymmetry is what produces every
per-machine result in the paper — the paired traces of Figure 14, the 21.1 %
DC-link split of Figure 13, and the terminal-voltage spread that grows as the
grid weakens. See [`tab01_benchmark_params.md`](tab01_benchmark_params.md).

## The sign convention

The figure carries an export reference direction: `P_g, Q_g` positive means
export, so **`P_g < 0` in the plotted traces** when the farm is generating. This
catches people out when comparing a grid-side trace against a machine-side one.

Measured on the archived sag run: machine `P = 0.7282` pu while grid-side
`P = −0.6647` pu. Same power flow, opposite sign, and the difference in
magnitude is the transformer and collector losses.

## Two nodes, and they are not the same node

- **Stator terminals**, where `|u_dqs|` is measured — the quantity Figure 14
  plots, and which differs per machine pair.
- **PCC**, where `V_pcc` is measured — one node, common to the farm.

The paper's operating points are specified at one or the other and the
distinction is load-bearing: the *designated* point is specified by the source
voltage `|v_g| = 1` pu, the *optimisation* point by `V_pcc = 0.975` pu. Neither
implies the other. See [`00_setup.md`](00_setup.md).
